title: Transplanting Meaning in Farming: What It Is and How DAT Is Counted
metaTitle: Transplanting Meaning in Farming and How DAT Is Counted
metaDescription: Transplanting meaning in farming: moving seedlings from a seedbed to the field. Compare it with direct seeding, see seedling ages, and learn how DAT counts.
excerpt: The transplanting meaning in farming is simple. You raise seedlings in a seedbed or tray first, then move them to the field. Palay, onion, tomato, eggplant and cabbage usually start this way. From that day on, farmers count the crop's age as DAT, or days after transplanting.

blocks.text:
On a lowland rice farm, the season turns on one day, when the seedlings leave the seedbed for the paddy. That day starts the count farmers use for fertilizer, water and pest checks.

In Tagalog, farmers call it lipat tanim, and direct seeding sabog tanim. This guide explains both. It also gives the right seedling age for each crop, ways to limit transplant shock and how to count DAT.

Transplanting is moving a young plant from where it started to where it will grow to harvest. In agriculture, it usually means moving seedlings from a seedbed, a tray or a nursery bag to the field.

That is the plain transplanting meaning a farmer uses. Transplanting in agriculture covers palay from a wet bed or a tray and vegetables like tomato and cabbage. It also covers fruit trees moved from nursery bags into holes.

items: Seedlings get a protected start in a small bed that is easy to water and watch.
The crop starts ahead of the weeds, because the field gets plants that are already weeks old.
The crop spends less time in the field, which helps fit two crops in a year.
It uses less seed, since nearly every seedling ends up in a hill.
You can choose only the strong seedlings and leave the weak ones behind.

blocks.text: Transplanting versus direct seeding for palay

blocks.caption: Transplanted and direct seeded rice compared
rows: About 20 to 40 kg for the seedbed
About 40 to 60 kg with a drum seeder, often more when broadcast
Heavy at transplanting, a crew for a day or more
Weeds and rice start together, so weed control matters more
Young seedlings are easy prey in the first weeks
Very level field with small drainage canals
Transplant shock costs a few days
Often ready a few days sooner from sowing

blocks.text: Neither one is always better. Where labor is scarce or costly, many farmers switch to direct seeding. Where weeds, snails or uneven fields are the bigger problem, transplanting often pays. Our guides to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) and [direct seeded rice land preparation](/land-preparation/direct-seeded-rice-land-preparation) show the field work for each.

Farmers usually transplant vegetables with small seeds and slow early growth. Tomato, eggplant, pepper, cabbage, broccoli, lettuce and onion are the common ones. Root crops like carrot and radish are sown straight in the field, because a moved root grows crooked. Beans and corn are also direct seeded.

Cucurbits like ampalaya, squash and cucumber have roots that dislike any disturbance. Still, many growers raise them in trays. Then they move them very young, about a week after sprouting, with the whole root ball. Before any transplanting, harden the seedlings for about a week. Water them less and give them more sun, so the move to the field is not a shock.

blocks.caption: Usual seedling age at transplanting, counted from sowing
rows: About 30 to 35 days, with 3 to 4 true leaves
About 25 to 35 days, short and sturdy
About 7 to 10 days after the seed sprouts

blocks.text: Old seedlings recover slowly and tiller or branch less, while very young ones break easily and drown in deep water. So time the seedbed sowing for the day the field and the crew will be ready.
Transplant shock and how to reduce it

Transplant shock is the setback a seedling suffers after the move. Roots tear, and the plant loses water faster than it can take it up. So it wilts or yellows for some days. Rice leaf tips may dry before new leaves come. Most seedlings recover within a week or so, but a hard shock delays the whole crop.

items: Water the seedbed the day before you pull, so the roots come out with less damage.
Transplant in the late afternoon or on a cloudy day, not in the midday heat.
Keep pulled seedlings in the shade and plant them the same day.
Plant rice shallow, only a few centimeters deep, so tillers start sooner.
Keep a ball of soil on vegetable roots, and water each plant right after planting.
Use seedlings of the right age, because younger ones bounce back faster.

blocks.text: How days after transplanting (DAT) is counted

DAT stands for days after transplanting. The transplanting day itself is DAT 0. The next day is DAT 1, and a week later is DAT 7. Before that day, while the seedlings are still in the seedbed, farmers count days after sowing, or DAS.

The two counts add up to the crop's real age. A seedling pulled at 21 days and now at 30 DAT is 51 days from sowing. This matters at harvest time. Rice maturity counts from sowing. So a 115 day variety with 21 day old seedlings is ready at roughly 94 DAT, or a few days later after a hard shock.

Most advice for transplanted crops uses DAT. For example, our [cropping calendar guide](/blog/how-to-make-a-cropping-calendar) puts the basal fertilizer at 0 to 14 DAT. The first top dressing follows at 22 to 26 DAT. Each lot keeps its own count, so a lot transplanted a week later gets each task a week later.
How anee.io counts DAT for every lot

anee.io counts every task from each lot's own transplanting day. While the seedlings are in the seedbed, a transplanted lot counts days after sowing. On its transplanting day, the count starts again at DAT 0. From then on, every task takes its date from that day. Two lots transplanted a week apart each get their own dates on the [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar).

When the crew runs late, drag the task to its new day. The delay counter shows any lot that runs behind. blocks.text: Questions about the transplanting meaning in farming

items.q: What does transplanting mean in farming?
items.a: It means raising seedlings in a seedbed, tray or nursery first. Then you move them to the field, where they grow to harvest. Farmers usually transplant palay, onion, tomato, eggplant and cabbage.

items.q: What is DAT in rice farming?
items.a: DAT means days after transplanting. It counts the days since the seedlings went into the paddy. Most fertilizer, water and pest advice for transplanted rice uses it.

items.q: Is transplanting day DAT 0 or DAT 1?
items.a: Transplanting day is DAT 0, and the next day is DAT 1. In anee.io, every lot counts the same way.

items.q: How old should rice seedlings be at transplanting?
items.a: Usually 18 to 21 days for hand transplanting and 14 to 18 days for a mechanical transplanter.
